QUESTION 2 Problem Solving Questions (15 marks)
A. Personal Financial Management
1. State one economic challenge and one social challenge faced by a young worker in managing personal finance. (2 marks)
2. Describe one way in which the challenges stated in (1) could be overcome. (1 mark)
questions.model:
1. Economic (1): rising prices/inflation; low wages; unemployment; high interest on loans. Social (1): family/cultural obligations (church, funerals, functions); peer pressure to spend; habits such as gambling or drinking.
2. Any one, described (1): prepare and follow a budget; save a fixed amount every pay; set priorities – needs before wants; avoid unnecessary borrowing; find extra income through an enterprise.

questions.text:
B. Managing Credit
1. Identify one formal (institutional) source of borrowing. (1 mark)
2. Give one disadvantage of using credit. (1 mark)
C. Managing Risk and Financial Planning
3. Differentiate between a premium and a claim. (2 marks)
questions.model:
1. Any one (1): commercial bank (BSP, ANZ, Westpac, BRED, HFC); Fiji Development Bank; credit union/cooperative; finance company; FNPF (housing/education withdrawal).
2. Any one (1): interest makes goods cost more; debt can build up; goods can be repossessed; bad credit record if payments are missed.
3. A premium is the amount the insured pays regularly to the insurer for insurance cover (1); a claim is the request made by the insured to the insurer for payment after a loss (1).

questions.text:
D. Investment in Financial Institutions
An advertisement from the Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) says: "Plan for your retirement – join today."
1. State a situation in which members of FNPF can withdraw their funds. (1 mark)
2. State two benefits you receive as an FNPF member. (2 marks)
3. The employee contribution rate is 8% of salary. Calculate how much you would contribute as an employee per year if your salary was $28 500 per annum. (2 marks)
questions.model:
1. Any one (1): retirement at 55; death (paid to nominees); permanent incapacity/medical; housing (first home/deposit); education; migration.
2. Any two (1 each): savings for retirement; interest earned on savings; housing assistance; education assistance; death/funeral benefit; medical assistance.
3. 28 500 × 8% = 28 500 × 0.08 (1) = $2 280 per year (1)

questions.text:
E. Financial Planning for the Future: Investment in Action
1. Identify one factor that influences an individual's investment decision. (1 mark)
2. Name two financial institutions in Fiji where students can save or invest. (2 marks)
questions.model:
1. Any one (1): level of risk; expected return/interest rate; amount of money available; length of time (liquidity); age and goals of the investor; advice received.
2. Any two (1 each): BSP, ANZ, Westpac, BRED Bank, HFC Bank, Fiji Development Bank, Unit Trust of Fiji, FNPF (voluntary), credit unions, Home Finance.

questions.text:
QUESTION 3 Paragraph Writing (5 marks)
Choose ONE question from the three questions given below and write a paragraph on it. The length of the paragraph should be between 75 and 100 words.
questions.model:
Option 1: Saving defined – part of income not spent and kept for future use (1); two reasons (1 each): emergencies, future goals (education, house), retirement, interest earned; two ways (1 each): budget, pay yourself first, open savings/term deposit account, cut wants.
Option 2: Two sources of income (1 each, max 2): wages/salary, allowance, business/enterprise profits, interest, rent; one impact of overspending (1); two ways to control spending (1 each): budget, shopping list, compare prices, avoid credit.
Option 3: Insurance defined – protection against financial loss, where the insured pays a premium and the insurer pays for covered losses (1); two types of insurance (1 each): life, medical, motor vehicle, house/fire, travel; two reasons why families need it (1 each).

choices.text:
"Saving a little every week builds a secure future." With reference to the statement:
• Define saving.
• Explain two reasons why young people should save.
• Discuss two ways to save regularly.

"Spend less than you earn." With reference to the statement:
• State two sources of income for a young person.
• Discuss one impact of spending more than you earn.
• Explain two ways to control spending.

"Insurance protects your family when the unexpected happens." With reference to the statement:
• Define insurance.
• Describe two types of insurance offered in Fiji.
• Explain two reasons why families should have insurance.

questions.text:
D. Measuring Periodic Income (7 marks)
Siosaia runs a canteen. He gave you this information for the year ended 31 December 2026:
Stock (1/1/2026) $3 200; Cash at bank $5 000; Purchases $6 500; Wages $900; Customs duty $180; Purchases returns $250; Sales $14 800; Sales returns $300; Freight inwards $120; Freight outwards $210; Stock (31/12/2026) $2 750
Required: Prepare the Trading Account of Siosaia for the year ended 31 December 2026 and show the Gross Profit.
questions.model:
Sales 14 800 less Sales returns 300 = Net sales 14 500 (1)
Opening stock 3 200 (½); Purchases 6 500 less Purchases returns 250 = 6 250 (1); add Customs duty 180 and Freight inwards 120 (1) → Cost of goods available 9 750 (½); less Closing stock 2 750 (1) → Cost of goods sold 7 000 (1)
Gross Profit = 14 500 − 7 000 = $7 500 (1) (heading/format ½ taken off if missing).
Wages, freight outwards and cash at bank do NOT go in the Trading Account.

QUESTION 2 Problem Solving Questions (15 marks)
A. Introduction to Economics
State one difference between a market economy and a traditional economy. (2 marks)
B. Microeconomics
i. State two factors that would cause a change in demand. (2 marks)
ii. Discuss one function of the Fiji Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC). (1 mark)
questions.model:
A. Market economy – decisions on what/how/for whom to produce are made by buyers and sellers through prices and the profit motive (1); traditional economy – decisions are based on customs, traditions and culture, often subsistence (1).
B i. Any two (1 each): income; price of related goods (substitutes/complements); tastes and fashion; population size; advertising; expectations of future prices; season/weather.
B ii. Any one (1): controls prices of essential items (price control); protects consumers from unfair trading; checks that businesses compete fairly; investigates complaints.

QUESTION 3 Paragraph Writing (5 marks)
Choose ONE question from the three questions given below and write a paragraph on it. The length of the paragraph should be between 75 and 100 words.
questions.model:
Option 1: Market economy defined (1); two features (1 each): private ownership, prices set by demand and supply, profit motive, competition, consumer sovereignty; one advantage (1) and one disadvantage (1) (e.g. efficiency/choice vs. inequality, essential services not provided).
